newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Chase HK$2 billion FRCD seen.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Chase HK$2 billion FRCD seen.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Bank will hit the market with a HK$2 billion floating rate certificate of deposit issue on Wednesday, arranger Chase Manhattan Asia said.
It gave no pricing details, but said the issue would be for three years, and it would seek eligibility to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) liquidity adjustment facility (LAF).
For possible comparison purposes, Standard Chartered Bank last week issued HK$2 billion in three-year FRCDs at par to float at 20 basis points over one-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Standard Chartered is also seeking LAF eligibility.
Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd launched its two tranche fixed/floating-rate 20 billion yen Samurai issues through Nikko Securities on Tuesday.
Both tranches were for 10 billion yen and mature in 2000, but tranche A was fixed and tranche B was floating rate.
Tranche A was issued at par and carried a 2.6 percent coupon, and Tranche B was issued at par to float at 90 basis points over six-month yen London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
It is believed to be one of only a handful of such Samurai issues to feature a dual fixed/floating structure.
Peregrine said it wanted to diversify its funding mix and increase long-term debt financing.
"That will help us to eliminate any of the refinancing risk on Peregrine's borrowing portfolio," said a source in Peregrine's treasury operations.
He said Peregrine also wanted to make use of its JBRI rating from Japan Bond Research Institute and take advantage of Japanese appetite for such issues.
Part of the issue proceeds have already been swapped into U.S. dollars, he said, giving no further details.
This week should see a US$150 million two-year floating-rate note (FRN) for Steady Safe Finance BV, a borrowing agency for an Indonesian bus operator.
CITIC Pacific's two-tranche HK$8.0 billion loan has been increased to HK$8.8 billion after being oversubscribed, one of the arrangers said.
PT Pan Indonesia Bank (Bank Panin), acting through its Cayman Islands branch, plans a US$65 million six-year FRCD, sole arranger Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp said.
The FRCDs include put and call options at the end of the third year, and are priced at par to float at 70 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 87 basis points over LIBOR in general syndication.
General syndication is expected to start next week after the formation of a co-arrangers group.
